name: Firefox
statusNote: Actively developed by Mozilla across desktop and mobile platforms.

ios.note: Official iOS app using Apple's browser-engine rules.

availability.cpuNotes: Official desktop builds cover common 64-bit architectures.
availability.installMethod: Official installer, Linux package, or app store.

foundation.codeLicense: Open source under Mozilla Public License 2.0 and compatible licenses

telemetry.note: Firefox offers telemetry and data-collection controls in settings.

trackerBlocking.note: Enhanced Tracking Protection blocks known trackers by default.

fingerprintingProtections.note: Enhanced Tracking Protection includes fingerprinting protection controls.

privacy.privateWindows: Private Windows discard local history and use stricter tracking protections; they are not anonymous browsing.

vpnOrProxy.note: A built-in browser VPN is rolling out regionally; Mozilla VPN remains a separate paid full-device service.

manifestV2.note: Firefox continues to document WebExtensions APIs with its own compatibility policy.

manifestV3.note: Firefox supports Manifest V3 with browser-specific API differences.

extensions.limitations: Chrome extensions are not a supported installation path; Firefox Add-ons compatibility is the relevant measure.

nativeContentBlocking.note: Enhanced Tracking Protection is native but is not equivalent to a universal ad-blocking promise.

verticalTabs.note: Vertical tabs are a built-in layout option, enabled from the tab strip or sidebar settings.

profiles.note: Profiles or equivalent browser identities are available.

splitView.note: A native Split View shipped in Firefox 149.

sidebar.note: Firefox includes a sidebar for bookmarks, history, and tabs.

commandPalette.note: Command palettes are available through add-ons.

sync.note: Sync is provided by the browser or its upstream project.

translation.note: Firefox Translation is available for supported language pairs.

pwa.note: Native taskbar web apps are Windows-only since Firefox 143; other desktops need an extension.

iosEngine.note: Apple permits alternative engines in the EU and Japan under entitlement; no non-WebKit build ships in the App Store.

assistant.note: AI chatbot sidebar and AI Controls provides a built-in assistant surface.

summarization.note: AI chatbot sidebar and AI Controls documents page or multi-tab summarisation.

aiSearch.note: Smart Window, documented as a beta, provides AI answers with live web results and cited sources.

modelChoice.note: AI chatbot sidebar and AI Controls documents a choice of models or local model support.

aiPrivacyControls.note: AI chatbot sidebar and AI Controls documents retention, training or kill-switch controls.

crossTabContext.note: AI chatbot sidebar and AI Controls documents awareness of multiple tabs or history.

voiceMultimodal.note: Voice or image interaction is not documented.

dataSaver.note: No documented data-saving or compression mode.

mobileExtensions.note: Add-ons install on Android from addons.mozilla.org through an in-app extensions manager; Mozilla states add-ons are unavailable on iOS.

setAsDefault.note: Mozilla documents the steps to make Firefox the default browser on both Android and iOS.

desktopSiteMode.note: Switching a page to desktop view is documented for both mobile builds.

downloadManager.note: Android documents a Downloads screen; the iOS pages cover saving files without naming a manager.

offlineReading.note: Reader View is documented; saving a page to read offline is not.

biometricLock.note: Android private tabs can be locked behind face, fingerprint, or PIN.

backgroundMedia.note: Background or picture-in-picture playback is not documented.

webPush.note: Web push support is not documented.
